findings.location: Definition 3.1 and Theorem 3.3, pp.11-12; nonempty open U, p.15; final deduction, p.17
findings.claim: The stated reducible-curve definition makes every pair intertwined, so the nonempty form of Theorem 3.3 used in the main proof is false.
findings.evidence: For arbitrary f,g choose fixed p,q and Z=({p}xP1) union (P1x{q}). It is a reduced pure one-dimensional invariant curve with both total projections surjective. For any f in a purported nonempty W_d, choose simple g outside its PGL2 orbit; this is possible because the simple open locus has dimension 2d+1>3. Thus all literal hypotheses hold but g is not conjugate to f.
findings.alternative_readings: If W_d is empty, the isolated theorem is vacuous, but cannot yield the explicitly nonempty U at p.15. Reading surjective componentwise adds a missing condition.
findings.impact: False central rigidity interface in the proof of Theorem 1.3; no counterexample to generic multiplier injectivity established.
findings.repair: Require finite projections, or a periodic irreducible component dominating both factors. The finite Corr objects on p.14 meet this stronger condition; a component of an invariant finite union is periodic, permitting the cited irreducible-curve theorem. Original definition must change.

findings.location: PCE/PR definitions p.12; Theorem 3.4 proof assertions (4),(5) and last paragraph p.14
findings.claim: Typicality assertions for every marked critical point are false under the theorem hypotheses and fail for the periodic critical points in the main constructed families.
findings.evidence: Take f_t=g_t=z^2+t over A1. Nonisotrivial, degree two, not flexible Lattes, infinitely many simultaneous PCF parameters. Infinity is a constant fixed critical section, with parameter derivative and distance to the critical set both zero for all iterates. Even the active constant section 0 has derivative zero at n=0. For a persistently periodic section c of period r, xi_{c,kr}=c, so exponential parameter growth is impossible along kr and PR fails.
findings.hypotheses: Infinite PCF parameters proved via P_1=t,P_{n+1}=P_n^2+t: for each prime p, degree 2^{p-1}, simple root 0, a further root gives exact period p. Distinct primes yield distinct parameters. Same family on both sides is allowed.
findings.impact: The asserted common full-measure set supplying inputs for the DAO step need not exist. This is a core proof issue; not a counterexample to Theorem 3.4 or to Theorem 1.3.
findings.repair: Apply pointwise conditions only to selected active a1,b1, allow a finite initial prefix or use iterated marked sections, and recheck the two-family renormalization with that convention. DAO p.52(b) already restricts to active points; its Definition 4.1 also has the n>=0 issue. No full replacement of the deep argument is certified here. Change b2 to b1 consistently.

findings.location: Lemma 3.5 proof, last two displayed inline formulas, p.16
findings.claim: Critical cycles and zero-multiplier fixed points are counted with different weights.
findings.evidence: For f(z)=z^2-1 on P1, critical cycles are infinity of length 1 and {0,-1} of length 2. u1=1,u2=3; printed inversion gives m2=2 although actual m2=1. Exact polynomial gcd checks independently verify u1..u4=(1,3,1,3).
findings.hypotheses: Degree two; f is hyperbolic PCF of disjoint type (1,2); choose g=f to satisfy the same-spectrum premise if needed.
findings.impact: The displayed reconstruction is false, but the lemma conclusion and critical-period detection survive the corrected formula.
findings.repair: u_n=sum_{l|n} l*m_l; m_n=(1/n)sum_{l|n} mu(l)u_{n/l}. A zero-multiplier fixed point is simple as a fixed point, so no additional algebraic multiplicity is needed.

focused_checks.reason: Primary read exact Definition3.1, Theorem3.3 and its proof on pp.11-12, the finite correspondence condition p.14, explicit nonempty U p.15 and final use p.17. For arbitrary f,g, fixed p,q exist on P1, and the union {p}xP1 with P1x{q} is reduced, pure one-dimensional, invariant with equality and has both total projections surjective. It satisfies the stated reducible-curve definition. For every f in any nonempty proposed W_d, the nonempty simple open in Rat_d of dimension 2d+1 contains g outside the <=3-dimensional conjugacy-orbit closure. Hence the nonempty rigidity assertion fails without assuming a numerical map belongs to an unknown generic set. Empty W_d makes the isolated wording vacuous but cannot supply the explicitly nonempty U. Primary read retained Pakovich2107.05963v2 pp.3,15: Theorem1.4 requires an irreducible nonhorizontal/nonvertical periodic curve; Lemma3.6 supplies generic simplicity. Finite projections on target p.14 ensure a component dominating both factors, and equality invariance permutes finitely many components, so a component is periodic and the cited theorem can be used with the subsequent entropy-rigidity step. This repairs the interface only after changing the definition. Major is supported by the main contradiction's dependency; no generic-injectivity counterexample is established.

Primary read the exact all-critical-point quantifiers and n>=0 in p.12, all Theorem3.4 hypotheses pp.13-14, and the persistently periodic critical relations pp.9-11,15. For f_t=g_t=z^2+t, nonisotriviality follows from fixed multiplier product 4t; degree2 excludes flexible Lattes and equality of families is allowed. P_p(t) has degree2^(p-1) with simple root0 and therefore another root for every prime p; this gives exact prime periods and infinitely many distinct simultaneous PCF parameters. Infinity is a fixed constant critical section with parameter derivative and recurrence distance zero at every iterate. A general persistently periodic section similarly has bounded derivative along multiples of its period and distance zero, so the claimed common full-measure PCE/PR set can be empty. Even active constant section0 fails the literal n=0 PCE bound. Primary read retained DAO2302.02583v2 pp.22-25,50-53: the conditions are for marked pairs, proof p.52(b) restricts to active critical points and Proposition7.8 to selected a,b. A passive zero activity measure cannot support almost-everywhere claims for the total nonzero measure. The source Definition4.1 also prints n>=0, so it does not itself cure the finite-prefix defect. Repair requires the selected active a1,b1, a justified finite-prefix or iterate convention, measure scaling and the two-family renormalization, plus b2/b1 consistency; a full deep replacement proof is not certified. The diagonal already intertwines the example, so neither Theorem3.4's intended conclusion nor generic injectivity is refuted.

Primary read p.16's explicit definitions of zero multiplier fixed points u_n and critical cycles m_l and checked the retained exact polynomial gcd calculation. A critical l-cycle contributes l distinct zero-multiplier fixed points of f^n precisely for l dividing n; these fixed points are simple because the local fixed-point equation has derivative -1. Hence u_n=sum(l*m_l) and Mobius inversion has factor1/n. For z^2-1 the fixed critical infinity and two-cycle0,-1 give u1=1,u2=3 and m2=1, whereas the printed formula gives2; choosing g=f meets the same-spectrum premise. Corrected inversion still recovers all lengths, and 2d-2 distinct superattracting cycles use the entire critical-point budget. Minor is appropriate and the lemma conclusion survives. Historical calculation executions are reused with original attribution.
